books.title: Pride and Prejudice
books.author: Jane Austen
books.description: A Regency-era novel of manners in which five women try to adjust to their new neighbor, an eligible gentleman.

books.title: Frankenstein

books.description: A tragic scientist creates a monster in his laboratory.

books.title: Moby Dick
books.author: Herman Melville
books.description: Captain Ahab, having lost his leg to the white whale Moby Dick, travels the world on a quest for vengeance.

books.title: Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland
books.author: Lewis Carroll
books.description: A young girl follows a white rabbit into a strange land of poetry, humor, and whimsy.

books.title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
books.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
books.description: The world’s first consulting detective investigates a variety of intriguing cases in the first Holmes short story collection.

books.title: Romeo and Juliet
books.author: William Shakespeare
books.description: The children of two opposing houses fall in love.

books.title: The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde
books.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
books.description: A London lawyer investigates the relationship between a brilliant scientist and a misshapen misanthrope.

books.title: Dracula
books.author: Bram Stoker
books.description: An ancient undead monster terrorizes Victorian London.

books.title: Little Women
books.author: Louisa May Alcott
books.description: The story of how four young sisters grow to adulthood.

books.title: The Odyssey
books.author: Homer
books.description: An epic poem following a Greek hero trying to return home after the Trojan war.

books.title: A Room With a View
books.author: E. M. Forster
books.description: A young English woman falls in love while on tour in Italy.

books.title: Middlemarch
books.author: George Eliot
books.description: In the neighborhood of a rural English town in the 1830s, several men and women struggle with love, marriage and fortune.

books.title: The Divine Comedy
books.author: Dante Alighieri
books.description: Dante journeys through Hell, Purgatory, and Heaven in order to receive salvation and to find divine love.

books.title: The Blue Castle
books.author: L. M. Montgomery
books.description: A young woman throws off the constraints of her dreary existence when she learns she has one year left to live.

books.title: Crime and Punishment
books.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
books.description: Inflated by his own ambition, an ex-student murders a pawnbroker, then faces the inevitable consequences.

books.title: The Diary
books.author: Samuel Pepys
books.description: The diary of a man living in London in the 17th century.

books.title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
books.author: Oscar Wilde
books.description: A Victorian dandy turns to a life of debauchery after a magical portrait stops him from aging.

books.title: Jane Eyre
books.author: Charlotte Brontë
books.description: A woman is hired by the mysterious master of Thornfield Hall as a governess for his young ward.

books.title: The Storm of Steel
books.author: Ernst Jünger
books.description: A German storm troop officer recounts his experiences in World War I.

books.title: Meditations
books.author: Marcus Aurelius
books.description: The personal diary of the Roman Emperor, in which he lays out his thoughts and philosophical musings on the Stoic philosophy and way of life.

books.title: Beowulf
books.description: A hero is hired to kill a monster that has been plaguing the land.

books.title: The Count of Monte Cristo
books.author: Alexandre Dumas
books.description: A man seeks revenge for having been falsely imprisoned years earlier.

books.title: A Tale of Two Cities
books.author: Charles Dickens
books.description: A family is reunited, added to, and then threatened to be torn apart by events arising from the French Revolution.

books.title: Sense and Sensibility
books.author: Jane Austen
books.description: Two sisters take long journeys to love in early nineteenth-century England.

books.title: The Great Gatsby
books.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
books.description: The decadent and mysterious Jay Gatsby pursues the American Dream in Jazz Age New York.

books.title: The Secret of Chimneys
books.author: Agatha Christie
books.description: A murder at a country house embroils its weekend guests in an international regicide, while a famous jewel thief may be lurking among them.

books.title: My Life
books.subtitle: Volume 1
books.author: Richard Wagner
books.description: An autobiography written between 1865 and 1880, covering his life from birth in 1813 to 1864. Dictated to his mistress Cosima von Bülow at the request of King Ludwig II of Bavaria, Wagner recounts his tempestuous career, friendships, and controversies in surprisingly frank detail. Originally printed in limited editions for private circulation, the memoir sparked rumors due to its restricted availability.

books.title: The Adventures of Tom Sawyer
books.author: Mark Twain
books.description: A young boy growing up in Missouri gets into all sorts of trouble and, with his friend, stumbles on a treasure.

books.title: The Prince
books.author: Niccolò Machiavelli
books.description: The classic treatise on how to tyrannize one’s subjects.

books.title: The Enchanted April
books.author: Elizabeth von Arnim
books.description: Four women spend a month-long holiday at a medieval Italian castle, where they find themselves renewed and transformed by the beauty around them.

books.title: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
books.author: L. Frank Baum
books.description: The adventures of a young farm girl named Dorothy in the magical Land of Oz, after she and her pet dog Toto are swept away from their Kansas home by a cyclone.

books.title: The Scarlet Letter
books.author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
books.description: A woman in the Puritan Massachusetts Bay Colony is forced to wear the shame of her sin embroidered on her clothes.

books.title: The Yellow Wallpaper
books.author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
books.description: A short story published in January 1892. This landmark work of feminist literature and horror fiction follows a woman confined to a nursery by her physician husband as treatment for "temporary nervous depression." Forbidden from working or writing, she documents her experience through secret journal entries. With nothing to occupy her mind but the room's disturbing yellow wallpaper, she descends into madness, becoming obsessed with its strange patterns and the figures she perceives within it.

books.title: Twenty Years After
books.author: Alexandre Dumas
books.description: Four musketeers are drawn back together by current events after many years apart, try to save Charles I from Cromwell, and are pursued by the now-grown son of a former female adversary.

books.title: The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire
books.author: Edward Gibbon
books.description: A narrative history of the Roman Empire from the time of Trajan to the fall of Constantinople.

books.title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
books.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
books.description: A famous detective investigates a mysterious and apparently supernatural threat to the heir of a wealthy Dartmoor estate.

books.title: Cranford
books.author: Elizabeth Gaskell
books.description: A series of sketches about small town life in a changing mid-Victorian England.

books.title: War and Peace
books.author: Leo Tolstoy
books.description: The story of five families in Russia during the Napoleonic Wars.

books.title: The Final Count
books.author: H. C. McNeile
books.description: An arch criminal tries to get his hands on the world’s deadliest poison.

books.title: The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn
books.author: Mark Twain
books.description: The adventures of a young boy and his friend, an escaped slave, on the Mississippi river in the Antebellum South.

books.title: The King in Yellow
books.author: Robert W. Chambers
books.description: Ten short stories of madness, hauntings, romance, and art.

books.title: The Iliad
books.author: Homer
books.description: The epic poem which follows a Greek warrior who refuses to give up his prize of war.

books.title: The Expedition of Humphry Clinker
books.author: T. Smollett
books.description: An epistolary novel published in 1771. Six correspondents—including a gouty Welsh squire, his husband-hunting sister, and their servants—chronicle a journey through England and Scotland's fashionable spa towns and resorts. Through wildly contrasting letters describing the same events, Smollett satirizes eighteenth-century British society, class pretensions, and urban life. The mysterious ostler Humphry Clinker joins their travels, bringing comic misadventures, romantic entanglements, and surprising revelations that transform the expedition.

books.title: The Adventures of Ferdinand Count Fathom
books.author: T. Smollett
books.description: A satirical novel written in the mid-18th century. The narrative follows the cunning and morally ambiguous character of Ferdinand Count Fathom, a man of mysterious parentage armed with an extraordinary talent for deception and manipulation. The story sets the stage for themes of vice and virtue, exploring Fathom’s escapades and schemes as he navigates a world ripe for exploitation. The opening of the novel introduces Fathom in an unusual light—born under strange circumstances to a mother who flitted between roles in military encampments and armies.

books.title: The History of Tom Jones, a Foundling
books.author: Henry Fielding
books.description: The adventures of an illegitimate young man and his pursuit of romance.

books.title: The Adventures of Roderick Random
books.author: T. Smollett
books.description: A picaresque novel published in 1748. Born to a Scottish gentleman and cast out by his family, young Roderick Random must survive by his wits alone in eighteenth-century Britain. From London to the West Indies, he encounters malice, deception, and hypocrisy at every turn while pursuing wealthy women and seeking his rightful place as a gentleman. Drawing on Smollett's own naval experience, this satirical tale exposes the brutality and corruption of its age.

books.title: The Return of Sherlock Holmes
books.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
books.description: The world’s first consulting detective returns to London after having faked his death some years before, and investigates a series of baffling mysteries.

books.title: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass
books.author: Frederick Douglass
books.description: Frederick Douglass describes his youth as a slave in Maryland and his desire to be a free man.

books.title: The String of Pearls
books.subtitle: Or, The Barber of Fleet Street. A Domestic Romance.
books.author: James Malcolm Rymer, Thomas Peckett Prest
books.description: A penny dreadful serial published from 1846 to 1847. This tale introduces Sweeney Todd, the murderous barber of Fleet Street who kills his customers and delivers their corpses to Mrs. Lovett, who bakes the flesh into meat pies. When a sailor mysteriously disappears after visiting Todd's shop, friends and loved ones investigate, uncovering a horrifying secret beneath St. Dunstan's church that reveals the true scale of Todd's crimes.

books.title: A Christmas Carol
books.author: Charles Dickens
books.description: A miserly moneylender is visited by four ghosts who help him see how to honor Christmas in his heart all year round.

books.title: The Confessions of St. Augustine
books.author: Augustine of Hippo
books.description: An autobiographical work written between AD 397 and 400. In thirteen books composed as prayers to God, Augustine recounts his turbulent journey from a sinful youth to Christian conversion. He reflects on his immoral past, his time following Manichaeism, and the influential figures who guided him toward faith. Considered the first Western autobiography, this intimate spiritual memoir explores themes of sin, redemption, and humanity's restless search for divine truth.

books.title: Great Expectations
books.author: Charles Dickens
books.description: An orphan boy living in Victorian England begins his life in extreme poverty and goes on to experience good fortune, love, rejection, wealth, and social challenges as he grows into adulthood.

books.title: Brigadier Gerard Stories
books.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
books.description: A gallant French cavalryman recounts his adventures in the Napoleonic Wars.

books.title: Grimms' Fairy Tales
books.author: Jacob Grimm, Wilhelm Grimm
books.description: A German collection of fairy tales first published in 1812. Beginning with 86 stories and eventually expanding to 210 tales across seven editions, this seminal work transformed oral folklore into written literature. The brothers collected stories from friends, acquaintances, and old books to preserve German cultural history. What started as a scholarly project evolved through decades of revisions, with tales added and removed, content adjusted for young readers, and illustrations incorporated to become a cornerstone of Western children's literature.

books.title: A Modest Proposal
books.subtitle: For Preventing the Children of Poor People in Ireland, from Being a Burden on Their Parents or…
books.author: Jonathan Swift
books.description: A satirical essay written and published in 1729. The work shockingly suggests that Ireland's poor could solve their economic troubles by selling their children as food to the wealthy. Through sustained irony and deadpan humor, Swift uses this outrageous premise to mock hostile attitudes toward the poor and expose the dehumanizing policies of British colonial rule. The essay remains celebrated for its dark wit and biting social commentary.

books.title: A Study in Scarlet
books.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
books.description: The self-declared world’s first consulting detective unravels a mysterious case of murder and revenge.

books.title: Leviathan
books.author: Thomas Hobbes
books.description: Hobbes explores a vision of the ideal state, in which people cede certain freedoms to a sovereign power in exchange for security and stability.

books.title: The Autobiography of Benjamin Franklin
books.author: Benjamin Franklin
books.description: Benjamin Franklin writes about his youth, adventures, and achievements.

books.title: Wuthering Heights
books.author: Emily Brontë
books.description: An adopted child ends up tearing apart families in a quest for power and revenge.

books.title: Moral Letters to Lucilius
books.author: Seneca
books.description: An elderly Roman Stoic philosopher gives life advice to a young friend.

books.title: Within and Without
books.author: George MacDonald
books.description: A spiritually unfulfilled monk goes on a journey to rescue a woman from his past.

books.title: Short Fiction
books.author: Edgar Allan Poe
books.description: A collection of Edgar Allan Poe’s short fiction, ordered by date of publication.

books.title: Treasure Island
books.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
books.description: A young boy finds adventure on the high seas as he battles bloodthirsty pirates in search of a long-lost treasure.

books.title: A Doll’s House
books.author: Henrik Ibsen
books.description: In 1870s Norway, a woman struggles to be herself within the confines of marriage and society.

books.title: Walden
books.author: Henry David Thoreau
books.description: Thoreau’s report on his social experiment of solitude, simplicity, and self-reliance.

books.title: Ulysses
books.author: James Joyce
books.description: A man passes a day in early twentieth-century Dublin, in a journey patterned on Homer’s Odyssey.

books.title: To the Lighthouse
books.author: Virginia Woolf
books.description: Over the course of a day—and again another day ten years later—the Ramsays and their friends plan a boating trip to the nearby lighthouse.

books.title: Anne of Green Gables
books.author: L. M. Montgomery
books.description: A coming-of-age story of a young girl growing up on a farm on Prince Edward Island.

books.title: The Swiss Family Robinson
books.author: Johann David Wyss
books.description: A Swiss family is shipwrecked on a remote island in the East Indies.

books.title: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow
books.author: Washington Irving
books.description: A short story written in 1820. Set in 1790 in a secluded glen near Tarrytown, it follows Ichabod Crane, a superstitious schoolmaster who competes with local rowdy Brom Bones for the affections of wealthy Katrina Van Tassel. After a harvest party filled with ghost stories about a Headless Horseman, Ichabod encounters a terrifying cloaked rider on his journey home. The next morning, he has vanished, leaving only mysterious clues behind.

books.title: The Importance of Being Earnest
books.author: Oscar Wilde
books.description: A comedy skewering Victorian high society.

books.title: Second Treatise of Government
books.author: John Locke
books.description: A political philosophy work published in 1689. Writing anonymously during England's turbulent revolution, Locke outlines a radical vision of society founded on natural rights and government by consent rather than divine authority. His ideas challenge the established order, arguing that legitimate power flows from the people, not kings claiming God-given rule. This foundational text of liberal political theory emerged from dangerous conspiracies and exile, so controversial that Locke never acknowledged authorship during his lifetime.

books.title: The Works of Edgar Allan Poe
books.subtitle: Volume 2
books.author: Edgar Allan Poe
books.description: A collection of literary works, including short stories and essays, written during the early to mid-19th century. This volume contains a range of tales that delve into themes of mystery, horror, and the uncanny, showcasing Poe's mastery of suspenseful and psychological storytelling. Notable pieces include "The Purloined Letter," which features the brilliant detective C. Auguste Dupin as he solves a complex crime involving a stolen letter of great importance, highlighting both the ingenuity of the detective and the folly of the authorities.

books.title: The Mysteries of Udolpho
books.author: Ann Radcliffe
books.description: A young woman experiences a series of unfortunate situations connected to an ancient castle.

books.title: The Brothers Karamazov
books.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
books.description: A dispute over inheritance between father and son escalates into a family feud.

books.title: The Murder of Roger Ackroyd
books.author: Agatha Christie
books.description: A legendary Belgian detective comes out of retirement to investigate a friend’s murder.

books.title: Gulliver’s Travels
books.author: Jonathan Swift
books.description: An Englishman travels to fictional islands where he meets tiny people, giants, magicians and talking horses.

books.title: The Call of Cthulhu
books.author: H. P. Lovecraft
books.description: A cosmic horror short story written in 1926 and published in 1928. After inheriting his grand-uncle's mysterious notes, Francis Wayland Thurston pieces together a terrifying puzzle involving disturbing dreams, ancient cults, and a monstrous entity called Cthulhu. His investigation leads him across continents, from New Orleans rituals to a nightmare city on an uncharted island, where something immense and ancient awaits. As Thurston uncovers the truth, he realizes he may become the next target.

books.title: The Souls of Black Folk
books.author: W. E. B. Du Bois
books.description: A seminal collection of essays on the African-American experience.

books.title: The Secret Garden
books.author: Frances Hodgson Burnett
books.description: A young girl is moved to the English countryside where she starts restoring a neglected garden, and uncovers secrets in the process.

books.title: Poirot Investigates
books.author: Agatha Christie
books.description: A calculating Belgian detective and his wide-eyed companion investigate and solve a series of mysteries.

books.title: The Murder on the Links
books.author: Agatha Christie
books.description: A famous Belgian detective and his sidekick are summoned to France to investigate the mysterious murder of a rich businessman.

books.title: The Turn of the Screw
books.author: Henry James
books.description: A governess moves in to a haunted manor.

books.title: Journey to the Center of the Earth
books.author: Jules Verne
books.description: Prompted by a mysterious Icelandic manuscript, a professor and his nephew, with the aid of a local guide, adventure to the center of the earth through the crater of a dormant volcano.

books.title: The Man in the Brown Suit
books.author: Agatha Christie
books.description: Anne Beddingfeld travels to South Africa after finding a cryptic note beside the body of a man whose death she witnessed in the London Underground.

books.title: Thus Spake Zarathustra
books.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
books.description: After ten years spent in solitude, Zarathustra goes back amongst men to share his accumulated wisdom and prepare humanity for the Overman.

books.title: The Problem of Cell 13
books.author: Jacques Futrelle
books.description: A short story first published in 1905. The tale features Augustus S. F. X. Van Dusen, "The Thinking Machine," who claims nothing is impossible when the human mind is properly applied. To prove his theory, he accepts an extraordinary challenge: escape from a prison cell within one week. This acclaimed mystery has been adapted multiple times for television, radio, and stage, and appears in numerous collections of greatest detective stories.
subjects: Augustus S. F. X. Van Dusen

books.title: Oliver Twist
books.author: Charles Dickens
books.description: A poor boy, born and raised in a workhouse in Victorian England, falls into the control of a gang of heartless criminals.

books.title: The Time Machine
books.author: H. G. Wells
books.description: A mysterious inventor travels to a land far off in time.

books.title: Carmen
books.author: Prosper Mérimée
books.description: A novella written and first published in 1845. In the lonely hills of Andalusia, a scholar meets a notorious outlaw named Don José, who tells the tale of his tragic downfall. His story revolves around Carmen, a captivating Romani woman whose fierce independence and refusal to be tamed leads to jealousy, violence, and death. This dark narrative of passion and fate later inspired Bizet's famous opera.

books.title: Whose Body?
books.author: Dorothy L. Sayers
books.description: An aristocratic detective unravels the mystery of a body deposited in a bathtub in 1920s England.

books.title: Beyond Good and Evil
books.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
books.description: Nietzsche’s philosophical treatise on the ambiguity of traditional morality.

books.title: The Republic
books.author: Plato
books.description: A Socratic dialogue written around 375 BC. Through conversations between Socrates and various Athenians, the work explores the meaning of justice and whether the just person is happier than the unjust. Socrates examines existing forms of government and proposes an ideal city-state ruled by philosopher-kings. The dialogue ranges across profound questions: the nature of the soul, the role of poetry, love, aging, and the purpose of political power itself.

books.title: The Interesting Narrative of the Life of Olaudah Equiano
books.author: Olaudah Equiano
books.description: An autobiography of an ex-slave in the mid 1700s.

books.title: Changeling, and Other Stories
books.author: Donn Byrne
books.description: A collection of short stories written in the early 20th century. The title story, "Changeling," introduces readers to Anna Janssen, a chorus girl on trial for the murder of her former lover, Alastair de Vries, as the courtroom drama unfolds with a backdrop of public scrutiny and personal transformation. The collection blends themes of crime, justice, and human relationships, and it appears to delve into deeper issues of identity and redemption.

books.title: Washington Confidential
books.author: Jack Lait, Lee Mortimer
books.description: A revealing and controversial exposé written in the early 1950s. This book offers a gritty look at the underbelly of Washington, D.C., exploring issues of corruption, vice, and the peculiarities of life in the nation’s capital. Through their journalistic lens, the authors promise an unfiltered narrative that challenges the sanitized image of Washington as the seat of political power. The opening of "Washington Confidential" sets the stage for this exploration by framing the city as a paradox.

books.title: The Man Who Was Thursday
books.author: G. K. Chesterton
books.description: An undercover policeman infiltrates a mysterious Anarchist group.

books.title: Les Misérables
books.author: Victor Hugo
books.description: An escaped convict steals two candlesticks and uses the proceeds to redeem himself and become an honest man.

books.title: Peter Pan
books.subtitle: $b [Peter and Wendy]
books.author: J. M. Barrie
books.description: A work that began as a play in 1904 and became a novel in 1911. It tells the story of Peter Pan, a mischievous boy who can fly and never grows up. He whisks Wendy Darling and her brothers away to Neverland, a magical island inhabited by mermaids, fairies, and pirates. There, they encounter the Lost Boys and face off against the villainous Captain Hook, all while navigating adventures that blur the line between childhood wonder and danger.

books.title: The Innocence of Father Brown
books.author: G. K. Chesterton
books.description: Amateur detective and Catholic priest Father Brown solves mysteries in this first collection of Father Brown short stories.

books.title: On Liberty
books.author: John Stuart Mill
books.description: Mill’s famous essay that applies a utilitarian ethical system to systems of government.

books.title: Heart of Darkness
books.author: Joseph Conrad
books.description: A steamer captain in the heart of Africa witnesses the final days of a brutal ivory trader.

books.title: The Mysterious Affair at Styles
books.author: Agatha Christie
books.description: A fastidious Belgian detective solves the mystery of a murder in an English country manor.

books.title: The Cruise of the Nona
books.author: Hilaire Belloc
books.description: Hilaire Belloc cruises around Wales and the English Channel on his sailboat, writing on a variety of topics.

books.title: Essays
books.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
books.description: A collection of Ralph Waldo Emerson’s essays.

books.title: Flower, Fruit, and Thorn Pieces
books.subtitle: Or, the Wedded Life, Death, and Marriage of Firmian Stanislaus Siebenkaes, Parish Advocate in the…
books.author: Jean Paul
books.description: A German Romantic novel published between 1796 and 1797. The story follows Firmian Stanislaus Siebenkäs, a public defender trapped in an unhappy marriage. When he consults his friend Leibgeber—who is actually his Doppelgänger—he receives radical advice: fake his own death to escape his miserable life. This darkly comedic tale blends satire with psychological depth, exploring the torn sensibilities of a man seeking both philosophical honesty and peace of soul in a stifling provincial world.

books.title: Paradise Lost
books.author: John Milton
books.description: A dramatic imagining in blank verse of the rebellion of Satan against God, Satan’s overthrow, and the Fall of Man.

books.title: The Works of Edgar Allan Poe
books.subtitle: Volume 1
books.author: Edgar Allan Poe
books.description: A collection of various literary works, likely written in the mid-19th century. This volume presents a comprehensive look at Poe’s contributions to the genres of horror, mystery, and poetry, showcasing his unique ability to navigate themes of melancholy and the supernatural. This collection includes not only the celebrated tales such as "The Murders in the Rue Morgue" and "The Tell-Tale Heart," but also illuminating prefaces and analyses of his life and works, inviting readers to delve into the mind of one of America's most iconic writers.

books.title: Emma
books.author: Jane Austen
books.description: A wealthy young woman decides to take on the role of patroness and matchmaker to a young protégé, with considerably less than successful results.

books.title: In Search of Lost Time
books.author: Marcel Proust
books.description: The first-person account of a man’s introspections on his life and examination of memory.

books.title: The Green Mummy
books.author: Fergus Hume
books.description: A novel likely written during the late 19th century. The story revolves around a young couple, Archie Hope and Lucy Kendal, as they navigate romance against a backdrop filled with mystery and intrigue, particularly centering on a rare mummy that Lucy's archaeologist stepfather, Professor Braddock, is eager to acquire. At the start of the novel, readers are introduced to Archie and Lucy, who share a playful yet serious conversation about their engagement.

books.title: The Phantom of the Opera
books.author: Gaston Leroux
books.description: A mysterious presence terrorizes the Paris Opera.

books.title: The Cask of Amontillado
books.author: Edgar Allan Poe
books.description: A short story first published in November 1846. Set during Carnival in an Italian city, it follows nobleman Montresor as he enacts revenge against fellow noble Fortunato for perceived insults and injuries. Told from the murderer's perspective, the tale lures Fortunato into the catacombs beneath Montresor's home with the promise of rare amontillado wine. What awaits is a carefully planned trap that ends in live burial. The story's central mystery lies not in detection, but in understanding Montresor's true motives for such extreme vengeance.

books.title: The Secret of Father Brown
books.author: G. K. Chesterton
books.description: The fourth set of stories of a Catholic priest who is also an amateur detective.

books.title: Demons
books.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
books.description: A small town becomes swept up in the fervor of attempted revolution.

books.title: At the Mountains of Madness
books.author: H. P. Lovecraft
books.description: An Antarctic expedition reveals the horrifying reality of ancient myths in the depths of the continent.

books.title: The Kama Sutra of Vatsyayana
books.subtitle: Translated From the Sanscrit in Seven Parts With Preface, Introduction and Concluding Remarks
books.author: Vatsyayana
books.description: An ancient Sanskrit text composed between the 3rd and 5th century CE. Rather than simply a manual on sexual positions, this Hindu work explores the art of living well, encompassing courtship, emotional fulfillment, maintaining relationships, and the philosophy of desire. Part of the broader Hindu concept of life's proper goals, it addresses when desire sustains happiness and how pleasure fits within a meaningful existence. The text combines terse aphoristic verses with prose, offering guidance on love's nature and the pursuit of satisfaction.

books.title: The Lives and Opinions of Eminent Philosophers
books.author: Diogenes Laërtius
books.description: Brief biographies of the prominent philosophers of ancient Greece.

books.title: The Memoirs of Sherlock Holmes
books.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
books.description: The world’s first consulting detective and his companion investigate further crimes and mysteries, culminating in a life-or-death struggle with an evil nemesis.

books.title: The Casebook of Sherlock Holmes
books.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
books.description: The world’s first consulting detective and his companion investigate further crimes and mysteries.

books.title: The Mystery of Edwin Drood
books.author: Charles Dickens
books.description: A young man mysteriously vanishes, and all the suspects are secretly in love with his fiancé.

books.title: The Monk
books.author: M. G. Lewis
books.description: A pious monk is led astray by a demon in disguise, while the son of a marquis tries to elope with a local nun.

books.title: The Wisdom of Father Brown
books.author: G. K. Chesterton
books.description: Amateur detective and Catholic priest Father Brown solves mysteries in this second collection of Father Brown short stories.

books.title: The Missing Will
books.author: Agatha Christie
books.description: A short detective story featuring the famous Belgian detective Hercule Poirot, written during the early 20th century. The narrative explores themes of intellect and determination as it follows Poirot as he investigates the unusual terms of a will left by a wealthy uncle to his niece. The story presents a delightful puzzle infused with Christie's trademark wit and clever plotting. In this tale, Poirot is approached by Miss Violet Marsh, the niece of the late Andrew Marsh, who challenges her intellect with a will that promises her inheritance only if she can outsmart him within a year.

books.title: Oedipus King of Thebes
books.subtitle: Translated into English Rhyming Verse with Explanatory Notes
books.author: Sophocles
books.description: An Athenian tragedy written around 429 BC. When a plague ravages Thebes, King Oedipus vows to find and punish the murderer of the previous king, Laius. As he investigates, the blind prophet Tiresias warns him to abandon his search. But Oedipus persists, unaware that his quest for truth will uncover devastating secrets about his own identity and past—secrets connected to an ancient prophecy about patricide and incest.

books.title: The Countess of Pembroke's Arcadia
books.author: Philip Sidney
books.description: A prose pastoral romance written towards the end of the 16th century. This ambitious work blends idealized shepherd life with dramatic tales of jousts, political intrigue, kidnappings, and battles. When a duke receives an ominous oracle predicting stolen daughters and a usurped throne, he retreats to a pastoral lodge—hoping to escape fate. Sidney significantly revised and expanded his original version before his death, creating two major texts that scholars call the Old and New Arcadia.

books.title: The Plymouth Express Affair
books.author: Agatha Christie
books.description: A crime fiction narrative written during the early 20th century. The story revolves around the famous Belgian detective Hercule Poirot as he investigates the mysterious murder of a young woman found dead in a train compartment. The narrative delves into the complexities of human relationships and the dark motives that can lead to crime. In this gripping mystery, Lieutenant Alec Simpson inadvertently discovers the body of the Honorable Mrs. Rupert Carrington on the Plymouth Express train.

books.title: The Hunter's Lodge Case
books.author: Agatha Christie
books.description: A crime fiction novella written in the early 20th century. This work is a captivating example of Christie's mastery in crafting intricate murder mysteries, centering around the famous detective Hercule Poirot. The story unfolds as Hercule Poirot, although recovering from influenza, is drawn into a puzzling case involving the murder of a wealthy man named Mr. Harrington Pace at a remote shooting lodge. The plot follows Captain Hastings, Poirot's loyal companion, as he is dispatched to investigate the murder after being contacted by Roger Havering, Pace's nephew.

books.title: Red Harvest
books.author: Dashiell Hammett
books.description: A hard-boiled detective arrives at a small mining town only to find his client murdered and the inhabitants embroiled in complex webs of corruption.

books.title: Poetry
books.author: T. S. Eliot
books.description: A collection of T. S. Eliot’s poetry, including “The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock,” “The Waste Land,” and “The Hollow Men.”

books.title: The Big Four
books.author: Agatha Christie
books.description: A famous detective must use all his little grey cells to stop an immensely powerful and ruthless organization from taking over the world.

books.title: Four Arthurian Romances
books.author: Chrétien de Troyes
books.description: A collection of medieval narratives written in the latter part of the 12th century. This work encompasses the stories of four heroes: Erec, Cligés, Yvain, and Lancelot, each exploring the themes of chivalry, romance, and adventure intertwined with the sophisticated ideals of courtly love. The romances reflect the rich tapestry of Arthurian legend, showcasing knights undertaking noble quests and engaging in battles for honor and love.

books.title: Le Morte d’Arthur
books.author: Thomas Malory
books.description: A late Middle Ages version of the story of King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table.

books.title: Narrative of the Captivity and Restoration of Mrs. Mary Rowlandson
books.author: Mary White Rowlandson
books.description: A memoir published in 1682. During King Philip's War, Rowlandson and her three children were captured by Native Americans after an attack on their Massachusetts settlement. Held for ransom for eleven weeks, she endured injury, separation from her family, and the death of her youngest daughter. Her account of survival, faith, and eventual release became one of America's first bestsellers and a foundational example of captivity narratives.

books.title: Weird Tales, Volume 1, Number 1, March 1923
books.subtitle: The Unique Magazine
books.author: Various
books.description: A pulp magazine published in 1923. Founded by J. C. Henneberger and J. M. Lansinger, this debut issue launched what would become a legendary publication in fantasy and horror fiction. Under editor Edwin Baird, the magazine introduced early works by writers who would shape the genre, including H. P. Lovecraft, Seabury Quinn, and Clark Ashton Smith. Despite initial financial struggles, this first issue marked the beginning of a magazine dedicated to unusual, supernatural stories that had never before found a specialized home.

books.title: The Woman in White
books.author: Wilkie Collins
books.description: A young drawing teacher falls in love with his aristocratic pupil, who falls victim to a devious plot to acquire her considerable fortune.

books.title: On the Origin of Species By Means of Natural Selection
books.subtitle: Or, the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life
books.author: Charles Darwin
books.description: A work of scientific literature published in 1859. It introduced the theory that populations evolve through natural selection, with life's diversity arising from common descent through a branching pattern of evolution. Darwin presented evidence from his Beagle expedition and years of research to challenge the belief that species were unchanging. The book sparked intense scientific, philosophical, and religious debate, ultimately transforming our understanding of life and becoming the foundation of evolutionary biology.

books.title: The Moonstone
books.author: Wilkie Collins
books.description: When a fabulous gem mysteriously goes missing, suspicion abounds and a hunt begins for the guilty party.

books.title: The Sign of the Four
books.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
books.description: An analytical detective is consulted by a young woman who has received a strange communication regarding her long-missing father and a mysterious treasure.

books.title: Short Fiction
books.author: H. P. Lovecraft
books.description: The complete U.S. public domain short fiction of horror legend H. P. Lovecraft.

books.title: Metamorphoses
books.author: Ovid
books.description: A collection of Greek and Roman myths that involve various forms of transformation.

books.title: Don Quixote
books.author: Miguel de Cervantes Saavedra
books.description: A mad knight-errant and his down-to-earth squire encounter adventure in the Spanish countryside.

books.title: The Extraordinary Adventures of Arsène Lupin, Gentleman-Burglar
books.author: Maurice Leblanc
books.description: An infamous French thief plans intricate ways of stealing precious paintings and jewellery in this first collection of Arsène Lupin short stories.

books.title: One Woman
books.subtitle: Being the Second Part of a Romance of Sussex
books.author: Alfred Ollivant
books.description: A novel written in the early 20th century. The book explores the lives and relationships of Ruth Boam and Ernie Caspar, a young couple recently married, as they navigate the challenges of love, family, and societal expectations in Sussex. Central to the story is their joy as newlyweds, contrasted with the complexities of their pasts and the shadowy figures that linger in their lives. The opening of the novel paints a vivid picture of Ruth and Ernie's quiet wedding day and the simple journey they undertake in a carrier's cart.

books.title: A Farewell to Arms
books.author: Ernest Hemingway
books.description: An ambulance lieutenant and a field nurse have an affair during World War I.

books.title: Around the World in Eighty Days
books.author: Jules Verne
books.description: On a bet, an eccentric Victorian gentleman races to circumnavigate the globe.

books.title: The Blue Lagoon
books.author: H. de Vere Stacpoole
books.description: After a shipwreck, two surviving children are stranded on an island paradise, experiencing its bounties and resources, facing the dangers of the natural world, and undergoing their own maturation and romance.

books.title: Weird Tales, Volume 1, Number 4, June, 1923
books.subtitle: The Unique Magazine
books.author: Various
books.description: A collection of short stories written in the early 20th century. This particular volume presents a variety of thrilling and chilling tales, showcasing the genre of weird fiction which often delves into the uncanny, the supernatural, and the bizarre. It features a range of characters, including intriguing figures like Colonel Knight and Ah Wing, who navigate treacherous circumstances filled with suspense and intrigue.

books.title: Life on the Mississippi
books.author: Mark Twain
books.description: A memoir and travel book published in 1883. It recounts Twain's experiences as a young steamboat pilot's apprentice on the Mississippi River before the Civil War, detailing the art of navigating the ever-changing waters. The second half chronicles his return journey decades later, observing how railroads, growing cities, and time have transformed the river and its culture. Blending personal history with tall tales and social commentary, Twain captures a vanishing era of American river life.

books.title: White Nights, and Other Stories
books.author: Fyodor Dostoyevsky
books.description: A collection of short stories written in the mid-19th century. The title story, "White Nights," revolves around an unnamed narrator who leads a solitary life in St. Petersburg and unexpectedly finds connection with a mysterious young woman named Nastenka. The collection explores themes of loneliness, longing, and the complexities of human relationships through the lens of Dostoyevsky's profound psychological insight. At the start of "White Nights," the narrator describes his feelings of desolation as he wanders through St.

books.title: Unnatural Death
books.author: Dorothy L. Sayers
books.description: An amateur detective’s investigation of the suspiciously-early death of an elderly lady triggers a series of deadly events.

books.title: The Secret Adversary
books.author: Agatha Christie
books.description: Tommy and Tuppence try to solve a mystery, only to find themselves embroiled in schemes of murder, millionaires, and diplomats.

books.title: The Art of War
books.author: Sunzi active 6th century B.C.
books.description: An ancient Chinese military treatise dating from the 5th century BC. Composed of 13 chapters, this influential work explores military strategy, tactics, intelligence operations, and the art of warfare. For nearly 1,500 years, it served as the lead text in China's Seven Military Classics. The treatise has shaped military thinking worldwide, inspiring leaders from Mao Zedong to Douglas MacArthur with its timeless principles of strategy and discipline.

books.title: Notes from Underground
books.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
books.description: A man living alone in St. Petersburg writes memoirs describing his alienation from modern society.

books.title: Hamlet
books.author: William Shakespeare
books.description: The ghost of the King of Denmark tells his son, Hamlet, to avenge his death.

books.title: The Home Book of Verse
books.subtitle: Volume 2
books.author: Burton Egbert Stevenson
books.description: A collection of poetry likely compiled in the early 20th century. This anthology features a rich variety of poems that center around the theme of love, showcasing the influence of historical and contemporary poets. Through various styles, the collection captures the essence of romantic and passionate experiences, offering readers a glimpse into the multifaceted nature of love. The opening of this volume introduces a selection of poems that explore love in its many forms, from the philosophical musings of Ralph Waldo Emerson to playful verses by poets such as Walter Raleigh and Shakespeare.

books.title: The Jungle Book
books.author: Rudyard Kipling
books.description: Seven fable-like tales about jungle animals in India and the humans who live on the edges of their realm.

books.title: The Mystery of the Blue Train
books.author: Agatha Christie
books.description: A retired detective finds himself at the scene of a murder aboard a French locomotive.

books.title: Catriona
books.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
books.description: After coming into his fortune and evading his uncle’s schemes, young gentleman David Balfour continues his adventures in 18th century Scotland, helping a politically unwelcome friend escape into France, avoiding the hangman himself, finding his place as a gentleman in Edinburgh society, and falling in love with the daughter of a notorious Macgregor clansman.

books.title: Orlando
books.author: Virginia Woolf
books.description: A young Elizabethan poet for whom success is elusive becomes a woman and embraces the spirit of the age.

books.title: The Call of the Wild
books.author: Jack London
books.description: The story of a domesticated dog’s return to a primitive state in the late 19th-century Yukon.

books.title: Short Science Fiction
books.author: Isaac Asimov
books.description: A collection of short science fiction by Isaac Asimov, ordered by date of original publication.

books.title: Manon Lescaut
books.author: Prévost abbé
books.description: A novel first published in 1731. It tells the tragic love story of a young nobleman and a common woman who choose to live together unmarried, beginning a moral descent into gambling, fraud, and crime. Their passionate relationship leads them from Paris to imprisonment and ultimately to deportation in New Orleans. Narrated retrospectively by the Chevalier des Grieux, this confessional tale shocked eighteenth-century readers with its realistic depiction of society's underbelly and became one of French literature's most reprinted classics.

books.title: The Thirty-Nine Steps
books.author: John Buchan
books.description: An expatriate returning to England after many years in South Africa is accused of a murder he did not commit, and has to flee from the police and other more dangerous pursuers.

books.title: The Bakhtyār Nāma
books.subtitle: A Persian Romance
books.description: A collection of Persian romantic tales written in the late 19th century, specifically aimed at English readers. This engaging work of fiction introduces readers to the story of Bakhtyār, a young man of noble birth raised by robbers, who faces wrongful accusations and strives to prove his innocence while navigating the intrigues of royal court life. The narrative intricately weaves themes of fate, loyalty, and the quest for justice amidst compelling character developments and challenges. The opening of "The Bakhtyār Nāma" sets the stage for a dramatic tale of royalty and treachery.

books.title: The Lesser Key of Solomon, Goetia, the Book of Evil Spirits
books.subtitle: $b Contains Two Hundred Diagrams and Seals for Invocation and Convocation of Spirits, Necromancy…
books.description: An anonymously authored grimoire compiled in the mid-17th century from older materials. This sorcery manual divides into five books, with the Ars Goetia cataloging seventy-two demons summoned through ritual magic. Drawing from Renaissance occult sources, the text details spirits, seals, and invocations for controlling supernatural entities. The work bridges medieval demonology and ceremonial magic, offering practitioners detailed instructions for summoning and commanding evil spirits through elaborate rituals and protective measures.

books.title: The Aeneid
books.author: Virgil
books.description: The legendary hero Aeneas flees the city of Troy with his father and young son, and travels to Italy to become the ancestor of the Romans.

books.title: Reminiscences of a Stock Operator
books.author: Edwin Lefevre
books.description: A roman à clef published in 1923. Told through the fictional Larry Livingston—inspired by legendary trader Jesse Livermore—the book chronicles decades of Wall Street triumphs and disasters. From exploiting bucket shops with massive leverage to navigating boom-and-bust cycles on the New York Stock Exchange, it reveals the psychological warfare of speculation. Called "a font of investing wisdom" by Alan Greenspan, this enduring classic captures an era when market manipulation was legal and fortunes vanished overnight.

books.title: An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations
books.author: Adam Smith
books.description: A treatise published in 1776. This foundational work of classical economics examines what builds nations' wealth at the dawn of the Industrial Revolution. Smith introduces revolutionary concepts like division of labor, free markets, and the "invisible hand" of self-interest guiding economic activity. Challenging the mercantilist policies of his era, he argues that supply and demand should determine commerce rather than government regulation, establishing theoretical foundations that would shape economic thought for centuries.

books.title: The Great God Pan
books.author: Arthur Machen
books.description: A horror and fantasy novella published in 1894. A dangerous experiment opens a young woman's mind to see the supernatural god Pan, with devastating consequences. Years later, mysterious deaths and suicides follow the beautiful but sinister Helen Vaughan wherever she appears. As investigators piece together her dark origins and unnatural powers, they uncover a terrifying truth linking her to the ancient pagan deity and the failed experiment that began it all.

books.title: The Seven Dials Mystery
books.author: Agatha Christie
books.description: A weekend party at a country mansion ends in murder, and the daughter of the lord of the estate joins Superintendent Battle in investigating.

books.title: Anna Karenina
books.author: Leo Tolstoy
books.description: A socialite starts an affair with a cavalry officer, against a backdrop of wealthy family life in Imperialist Russia.

books.title: A Midsummer Night’s Dream
books.author: William Shakespeare
books.description: This comedy follows four lovers and a thespian who become bewitched by fairies.

books.title: Daughters of Nijo
books.subtitle: A Romance of Japan
books.author: Onoto Watanna
books.description: A novel likely written in the early 20th century. This work delves into the entwined lives of its characters against the backdrop of Japanese nobility during a time of political and social change. Central to the narrative are two women from vastly different backgrounds: the lowly farmer’s daughter, Ohano, whose life is upturned by her kidnapping and forced into a life at the court, and the noble Princess Sado-ko, whose innocence and sheltered upbringing contrast sharply with the intrigues around her.

books.title: The Secret Agent
books.author: Joseph Conrad
books.description: A spy in London is ordered to stage a bombing to foment political and social chaos.

books.title: The Enchiridion
books.author: Epictetus
books.description: A manual of Stoic ethical advice compiled in the early 2nd century by Arrian, a disciple of the Greek philosopher. This concise handbook distills practical precepts for achieving mental freedom and happiness in all circumstances. It teaches readers to distinguish between what lies within their control and what does not, emphasizing that judgments, not external events, disturb people. Through vivid imagery and everyday examples, the work guides students toward flourishing in both favorable and adverse situations by developing the capacities of the human spirit.

books.title: The Life and Adventures of Robinson Crusoe
books.author: Daniel Defoe
books.description: Shipwrecked on a remote tropical island, a resourceful Englishman manages to survive alone for many years.

books.title: The Sorrows of Young Werther
books.author: J. W. von Goethe
books.description: Goethe’s first major work, a novel of unrequited love, longing, and deterioration into sorrow.

books.title: The Travels of Marco Polo
books.subtitle: Volume 1
books.author: Marco Polo, Rusticiano da Pisa
books.description: A 13th-century travelogue written between 1298-1299. This legendary account chronicles Polo's epic journey through Asia from 1271 to 1295 and his remarkable experiences at the court of Kublai Khan. Dictated by the Venetian explorer to romance writer Rustichello while imprisoned in Genoa, the book blends adventure with observation, revealing distant lands Europeans had never imagined. From its first appearance, readers have debated its authenticity—wondering whether these tales of marvels are truth or fantasy.

books.title: A Connecticut Yankee in King Arthur’s Court
books.author: Mark Twain
books.description: An engineer from 19th-century Connecticut is sent back in time to King Arthur’s medieval England.

books.title: The War of the Worlds
books.author: H. G. Wells
books.description: The first-person narrative of the Martian invasion of 19th-century Earth.

books.title: Mr. Standfast
books.author: John Buchan
books.description: An army general chases a network of German spies through Scotland, the Swiss Alps, and the First World War’s Western Front.

books.title: The Romance of Lust
books.subtitle: A Classic Victorian Erotic Novel
books.author: Anonymous
books.description: A four-volume novel written between 1873-1876. Narrated by Charlie Roberts, the work chronicles his sexual experiences beginning in adolescence and continuing through various encounters with family members, governesses, and acquaintances. The novel explores numerous taboo subjects and sexual practices of Victorian society. Scholars have debated its authorship, with William Simpson Potter and Edward Sellon as likely candidates. Steven Marcus famously coined the term "pornotopia" to describe its sexually charged world.

books.title: Tales of Terror and Mystery
books.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
books.description: A collection of short stories written during the late 19th century. The book delves into supernatural and mysterious themes, showcasing a range of tales that evoke both intrigue and horror. Each story explores human fears and the unknown, offering readers a blend of psychological insight and thrilling suspense. The opening of the book begins with "The Horror of the Heights," where the narrative focuses on an aviator, Joyce-Armstrong, who discovers a terrifying phenomenon while attempting to break altitude records in his aeroplane.

books.title: The Prince and the Pauper
books.author: Mark Twain
books.description: The Prince of England and a pauper find their identities switched.

books.title: Apology
books.author: Plato
books.description: A Socratic dialogue written after 399 BC. It presents Socrates's legal defense at his trial, where he faced charges of corrupting Athens's youth and introducing new gods. Standing before a jury of perhaps 500 Athenian men, Socrates refuses to use sophisticated rhetoric, speaking instead in his characteristic questioning style. Rather than compromise his integrity to avoid death, he challenges his accusers and maintains his philosophical principles, insisting his only wisdom comes from knowing that he knows nothing.

books.title: As You Like It
books.author: William Shakespeare
books.description: Forced to flee to the Forest of Arden, the daughter of a duke encounters a variety of characters, her banished father, and even finds love.

books.title: The Lady of the Lake
books.author: Walter Scott
books.description: A narrative poem first published in 1810. Set in the Scottish Highlands, it weaves together three dramatic plots: a romantic rivalry among three men vying for Ellen Douglas's love, a conflict between an exiled noble and King James V of Scotland, and a brewing war between Lowland and Highland forces. This influential work unfolds across six cantos, each capturing a single day's action in the wild Trossachs region, where love, loyalty, and ancient feuds collide.

books.title: Dubliners
books.author: James Joyce
books.description: Fifteen short stories about middle-class life in early 20th-century Dublin.

books.title: Thuvia, Maid of Mars
books.author: Edgar Rice Burroughs
books.description: When the beautiful Princess Thuvia of Ptarth is kidnapped, suspicion falls on John Carter’s son Carthoris, who sets out to rescue the woman he loves.

books.title: Simple Sabotage Field Manual
books.author: United States. Office of Strategic Services
books.description: A historical publication written during the early 1940s, amid World War II. This manual acts as a guide for ordinary civilians to conduct simple acts of sabotage against enemy operations without the need for specialized training or equipment. Its main topic revolves around promoting small, accessible forms of resistance that could collectively disrupt the enemy's war effort. The manual outlines various strategies and techniques for citizens to engage in sabotage that could be executed discreetly and with minimal risk.

books.title: The Valley of Fear
books.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
books.description: The final novel in Sir Arthur Conan Doyle’s Sherlock Holmes series follows the eponymous hero as he investigates a Sussex murder seemingly connected with a secret society.

books.title: De Profundis
books.author: Oscar Wilde
books.description: A letter written between January and March 1897 during his imprisonment in Reading Gaol. Addressed to his former lover Lord Alfred Douglas, the letter reflects on their tumultuous relationship and the extravagance that led to Wilde's conviction for gross indecency. In its pages, Wilde examines both Douglas's vanity and his own failings, then charts his spiritual transformation in prison and profound identification with Christ as a romantic artist. Written under strict supervision, the complete text wasn't published until decades after Wilde's death.

books.title: The Insidious Dr. Fu-Manchu
books.author: Sax Rohmer
books.description: An intrepid detective hunts the criminal mastermind Fu-Manchu through early 20th-century London.

books.title: Incidents in the Life of a Slave Girl, Written by Herself
books.author: Harriet A. Jacobs
books.description: An autobiography published in 1861. Written under the pseudonym Linda Brent, Jacobs recounts her experiences as an enslaved woman and mother who endured sexual abuse and years of hiding before escaping to freedom. She addresses Northern white women directly, revealing the particular horrors faced by enslaved mothers and challenging prevailing notions of womanhood that excluded Black women from their protection.

books.title: Winnie-the-Pooh
books.author: A. A. Milne
books.description: A father tells stories to his son about the son’s stuffed animals come to life.

books.title: David Copperfield
books.author: Charles Dickens
books.description: The semi-autobiographical tale of a young boy who rises up to become a successful novelist.

books.title: The Notebooks of Leonardo Da Vinci
books.author: Leonardo da Vinci
books.description: A comprehensive collection of writings and sketches that delve into various aspects of art and science, first compiled in the late 19th century. The notebooks reveal Leonardo's insights and observations on topics such as painting techniques, perspective, anatomy, and natural phenomena, reflecting the innovative spirit of the Renaissance era. The content spans approximately thirty years of Leonardo's intellectual labor, showcasing his analytical approach to understanding the world.

books.title: Bleak House
books.author: Charles Dickens
books.description: A young woman of uncertain parentage is taken in by a kindly guardian, while her fate and that of two other young people hinge on the outcome of an interminable legal case.

books.title: Love’s Labour’s Lost
books.author: William Shakespeare
books.description: A king and his men swear to abstain from women, just as four women arrive for a state visit.

books.title: The Awakening
books.author: Kate Chopin
books.description: A woman’s dawning realisation of her situation leads to a struggle for independence.

books.title: A Pair of Blue Eyes
books.author: Thomas Hardy
books.description: A vicar’s daughter becomes engaged to two men, and has not told them of each other.

books.title: The Prophet
books.author: Kahlil Gibran
books.description: A collection of prose poetry on themes such as love, beauty, and religion.

books.title: The Wind in the Willows
books.author: Kenneth Grahame
books.description: Four animals adventure through the bucolic English countryside.

books.title: Autobiography of a Yogi
books.author: Paramahansa Yogananda
books.description: A spiritual autobiography published in 1946. It chronicles Yogananda's journey from childhood in India through his search for his guru, his establishment of Kriya Yoga meditation teachings, and his travels to America where he lectured and founded the Self-Realization Fellowship. The book introduces Eastern spiritual wisdom and methods of God-realization to Western readers, featuring encounters with saints, scientists, and spiritual figures across two continents. Designated one of the most important spiritual books of the twentieth century, it has sold millions of copies worldwide.

books.title: Through the Looking-Glass
books.author: Lewis Carroll
books.description: In a follow-up to her adventures in Wonderland, Alice finds herself in a mirror image of the whimsical land where she becomes a queen in her own right.

books.title: Sonnets from the Portuguese
books.author: Elizabeth Barrett Browning
books.description: A collection of 44 love sonnets.

books.title: Dialogues
books.author: Seneca
books.description: Seneca’s dialogues and consolations, including “On Benefits,” examine living life through the lens of Stoic philosophy.

books.title: Poetry
books.author: Edgar Allan Poe
books.description: A collection of Edgar Allan Poe’s poetry.

books.title: His Last Bow
books.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
books.description: The world’s first consulting detective and his faithful biographer tackle more mysterious cases.

books.title: Twenty Thousand Leagues under the Sea
books.author: Jules Verne
books.description: A science fiction adventure novel serialized from 1869 to 1870. When ships worldwide report encounters with a mysterious sea monster, an American expedition sets out to destroy it. Professor Aronnax, harpooner Ned Land, and servant Conseil discover the creature is actually a futuristic submarine commanded by the enigmatic Captain Nemo. Held captive aboard the Nautilus, they embark on an extraordinary underwater journey, witnessing marvels and mysteries beneath the waves while uncovering their captor's dark past.

books.title: Notes from the Underground
books.author: Fyodor Dostoyevsky
books.description: A novella published in 1864. This confession-style narrative follows a bitter, isolated former civil servant in St. Petersburg known as the Underground Man. Through philosophical monologues and personal anecdotes, he attacks determinism and utopian ideals, arguing that humans need suffering and irrationality to maintain freedom. He obsesses over past humiliations and social encounters, embracing spite and inaction while despising the rational self-interest that he believes has trapped him in unhappiness.

books.title: The Elements of Style
books.author: William Strunk
books.description: A style guide first published in 1920. This compact manual distills the essentials of clear English prose into rules about grammar, punctuation, composition, and word usage. Strunk's original "little book" urged writers to omit needless words and embrace brevity. Later enlarged by his former student E. B. White in 1959, it became the influential writing guide known as "Strunk & White," selling millions of copies and shaping generations of American writers with its prescriptive approach to craft.

books.title: Songs of Innocence and of Experience
books.author: William Blake
books.description: A collection of illustrated poems combined in 1794. Blake hand-engraved, printed, and colored unique artwork to accompany each poem, exploring childhood innocence and experience as contrary states of the human soul. Originally published as separate volumes, the combined work shows pastoral harmony alongside subtle dangers of naiveté. Each page features distinctive illustrations that intensify the poems' meanings, making Blake's vision inseparable from both visual art and verse. The collection became a hallmark of Romanticism and has inspired countless musical adaptations.

books.title: Love and Freindship [sic]
books.author: Jane Austen
books.description: "Love and Freindship" [sic] by Jane Austen is a juvenile story written in 1790. Composed when Austen was just fourteen years old, this epistolary tale brilliantly parodies the romantic novels of sensibility popular in her era. Through letters from the heroine Laura, Austen lampoons the absurd conventions of sentimental fiction—fainting spells, wild coincidences, and exaggerated emotions. The story follows Laura's whirlwind marriage, unlikely family reunions, and dramatic misfortunes, showcasing the sharp wit that would define Austen's later masterpieces.

books.title: Carmilla
books.author: Joseph Sheridan Le Fanu
books.description: A Gothic novella published in 1872. A foundational work of vampire literature that predated "Dracula" by 25 years, it tells the story of young Laura, who lives in an isolated Austrian castle. When the enigmatic Carmilla arrives after a carriage accident, the two girls form an intense friendship marked by romantic advances and unsettling mysteries. As young women in nearby towns begin dying from an unknown illness, Laura experiences disturbing nightmares and her health mysteriously declines.

books.title: The Riddle of the Sands
books.author: Erskine Childers
books.description: Two English friends go on a sailing trip that quickly turns thrilling as they stumble upon a sinister German plot.

books.title: The Mystery of the Yellow Room
books.author: Gaston Leroux
books.description: A young reporter struggles to investigate a seemingly impossible crime, in which an assailant has escaped from a locked bedroom completely unseen.

books.title: Uncle Tom’s Cabin
books.author: Harriet Beecher Stowe
books.description: The account of several slaves who are sold to new owners after their current owner experiences financial hardship.

books.title: Discourses
books.author: Epictetus
books.description: Epictetus instructs his students how to live the life of a Stoic.

books.title: Nicomachean Ethics
books.author: Aristotle
books.description: Aristotle examines how one may live in the most thriving, excellent manner.

books.title: Symposium
books.author: Plato
books.description: A Socratic dialogue written between 385-370 BC. At a banquet in ancient Athens, notable figures including Socrates, Alcibiades, and Aristophanes engage in a contest of speeches praising Eros, the god of love. Each man offers his perspective on love's nature and power—from inspiring battlefield courage to transcending earthly desire. Through conflicting ideas and shifting viewpoints, the dialogue explores love's deepest meanings while showcasing both philosophical depth and literary artistry.

books.title: Common Sense
books.author: Thomas Paine
books.description: A pamphlet published in January 1776 advocating independence from Great Britain for the Thirteen Colonies. Written in clear, persuasive prose, Paine presents moral and political arguments to encourage common people to fight for egalitarian government. Published anonymously at the American Revolution's beginning, it became an immediate sensation—the best-selling American title of all time. Paine connected independence with Protestant beliefs and structured his work like a sermon, making the first serious case for full independence when reconciliation still dominated colonial thinking.

books.title: The Problems of Philosophy
books.author: Bertrand Russell
books.description: A beginner’s guide to problems in various fields of philosophy.

books.title: Candide
books.author: Voltaire
books.description: A witty satire that tells of the young Candide’s attempts to stay optimistic through a series of incredible hardships.

books.title: Philosophical Works
books.author: René Descartes
books.description: A collection of philosophical works.

books.title: Erotica Romana
books.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
books.description: A collection of 24 elegiac poems written during the late 18th century. The work draws inspiration from classical Roman poets such as Tibullus and Catullus, exploring themes of love, desire, and beauty within the scenic backdrop of Rome. The text is characterized by a sensuous and introspective tone, reflecting Goethe's experiences and contemplations during his time in Italy. The poems within "Erotica Romana" present a rich tapestry of romantic exploration, featuring a narrator who navigates both the physical and emotional landscapes of love.

books.title: The Tale of Peter Rabbit
books.author: Beatrix Potter
books.description: A children's book written and illustrated in 1893. The story follows mischievous young Peter Rabbit, who disobeys his mother's warning and sneaks into Mr. McGregor's vegetable garden. What begins as a quest for fresh vegetables quickly becomes a dangerous chase, as Peter must outwit the garden's owner to escape alive. His father wasn't so lucky—Mrs. McGregor baked him into a pie. Will Peter make it home safely, or will he share his father's fate?

books.title: The Lock and Key Library
books.subtitle: Classic Mystery and Detective Stories: Modern English
books.description: "The Lock and Key Library: Classic Mystery and Detective Stories: Modern English" edited by Julian Hawthorne is a collection of classic mystery and detective stories compiled in the early 20th century. This anthology features notable authors such as Rudyard Kipling, A. Conan Doyle, and Wilkie Collins, showcasing suspenseful tales that delve into crime, the supernatural, and the intricacies of human nature. The book offers a glimpse into the genre’s evolution, reflecting social conditions and the human psyche through its distinctive narratives.

books.title: Black Beauty
books.author: Anna Sewell
books.description: A memoir narrated by a horse whose idyllic time on an English farm prepares him for a life filled with constant change and varied circumstances.

books.title: Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus
books.author: Ludwig Wittgenstein
books.description: One of the most important texts of 20th century philosophy, in which the nature of the philosophy, language, understanding, and logical atomism are explored.

books.title: Undine
books.author: Friedrich Heinrich Karl La Motte-Fouqué
books.description: A romantic fairy tale novel written in the early 19th century. The story follows Undine, a water sprite, and her encounters with humans, particularly focusing on her relationship with Sir Huldbrand of Ringstetten. The narrative delves into themes of love, sacrifice, and the quest for a soul, addressing the nature of humanity through the lens of supernatural elements. The beginning of "Undine" introduces the idyllic setting of a picturesque cottage by a lake, where a fisherman lives with his aged wife. Their life is disrupted by the arrival of a knight, Sir Huldbrand, who is seeking shelter.

books.title: The Red House Mystery
books.author: A. A. Milne
books.description: An amateur sleuth visiting a country house solves the mystery of who shot the man in the locked room.

books.title: Mrs. Dalloway
books.author: Virginia Woolf
books.description: As Clarissa Dalloway walks through London on a glorious June day, her movements bring together a cast of friends and strangers, each in turn weighing matters of mind and heart.

books.title: Persuasion
books.author: Jane Austen
books.description: A young woman meets again with a lover whose marriage proposal she had been persuaded to reject several years ago.

books.title: The Critique of Pure Reason
books.author: Immanuel Kant
books.description: A philosophical work published in 1781. Kant investigates the limits and scope of metaphysics, asking how we can know anything before experiencing it. He challenges both rationalist and empiricist traditions, introducing revolutionary ideas about space, time, and knowledge. The central question driving the work is: "How are synthetic a priori judgments possible?" Kant argues this matter is crucial to the survival of human reason itself.

books.title: Macbeth
books.author: William Shakespeare
books.description: An ambitious general murders the King of Scotland and takes the throne for himself—and then he must deal with the consequences.

books.title: The Tragical History of Doctor Faustus
books.author: Christopher Marlowe
books.description: Dr. Faustus sells his soul to Lucifer in return for magical powers.

books.title: The Genealogy of Morals
books.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
books.description: Three essays analyzing the origins, meaning, and value of the concepts of good, evil, and bad; of guilt, punishment, and bad conscience; and of ascetic ideals, including those of truth and truthfulness.

books.title: Short Fiction
books.author: H. G. Wells
books.description: A collection of short stories by H. G. Wells in a variety of genres ordered by date of publication.

books.title: Short Fiction
books.author: Ray Bradbury
books.description: A collection of science fiction and fantasy stories by Ray Bradbury ordered by date of publication.

books.title: A Journey to the Centre of the Earth
books.author: Jules Verne
books.description: A science fiction novel first published in 1864. Professor Otto Lidenbrock, an eccentric German scientist, discovers a cryptic message suggesting a path to Earth's center through an Icelandic volcano. He embarks on an extraordinary expedition with his nephew Axel and guide Hans, descending into the depths below. The trio encounters underground oceans, prehistoric creatures, and countless perils as they journey through a hidden world beneath our feet, ultimately facing an explosive return to the surface.

books.title: Aesop's Fables
books.subtitle: A New Translation
books.author: Aesop
books.description: A collection of fables credited to a storyteller who lived in ancient Greece between 620 and 564 BCE. These short tales feature talking animals and plants that teach moral lessons through simple scenarios. Originally part of oral tradition, the fables were collected centuries after Aesop's death and have continuously expanded to include stories from diverse sources across time and cultures, becoming timeless tools for ethical instruction.

books.title: Camille (La Dame aux Camilias)
books.author: Alexandre Dumas
books.description: A novel first published in 1848. This semi-autobiographical story follows the tragic romance between Marguerite Gautier, a Parisian courtesan suffering from consumption, and Armand Duval, a young bourgeois who falls deeply in love with her. When Armand convinces her to leave her former life behind, their idyllic countryside existence faces interference from his disapproving father, concerned about family scandal. The tale explores forbidden love, sacrifice, and the harsh morals of 19th-century French society.

books.title: The Three Musketeers
books.author: Alexandre Dumas
books.description: A young Gascon moves to Paris to join the King’s Musketeers where he starts to investigate the kidnapping of his landlord’s wife.

books.title: Love-at-arms
books.subtitle: $b Being a Narrative Excerpted from the Chronicles of Urbino, During the Dominion of the High and…
books.author: Rafael Sabatini
books.description: A historical novel set during the late 15th to early 16th century, a tumultuous time in Italian history marked by political intrigue and power struggles among the noble houses. The story revolves around Francesco del Falco, the Count of Aquila, who becomes embroiled in conspiracy and treachery as he is approached by nobles seeking to dethrone Gian Maria Sforza, the self-indulgent Duke of Babbiano. The narrative promises themes of loyalty, ambition, and the conflicts between personal integrity and political duty.

books.title: The Phantom 'Rickshaw, and Other Ghost Stories
books.author: Rudyard Kipling
books.description: A collection of short stories first published in 1888. The volume presents four tales set in colonial India, ranging from supernatural hauntings to darkly adventurous encounters. A spurned lover returns as a ghost in her phantom rickshaw, mysterious billiard games echo in empty rooms, an Englishman becomes trapped in a village of the living dead, and two adventurers pursue a dangerous dream of kingship in remote Kafiristan. Each story explores the unsettling boundaries between reality and the otherworldly.

books.title: The Communist Manifesto
books.author: Karl Marx, Friedrich Engels
books.description: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels’ classic analysis of modern industrial society and call for Working Class revolution.

books.title: Northanger Abbey
books.author: Jane Austen
books.description: A young girl with an overactive imagination comes of age.

books.title: The Secret of the Night
books.author: Gaston Leroux
books.description: A novel written during the late 19th century. The story appears to unveil a tale of mystery and intrigue that revolves around General Trebassof, a figure embroiled in the tensions of revolutionary Russia, and the imminent threats against his life. The narrative introduces key characters such as Matrena Petrovna, the general's protective wife, and Joseph Rouletabille, a young reporter sent to investigate the dark circumstances surrounding the general’s fate.

books.title: The Yeoman Adventurer
books.author: George W. Gough
books.description: A historical novel likely written in the early 20th century. The story unfolds through the experiences of Oliver Wheatman, a yeoman, as he navigates life in a tumultuous period marked by the Jacobite uprisings, personal ambition, and romantic entanglements. The novel delves into themes of bravery, identity, and the quest for adventure against a backdrop of deep social and political upheaval.

books.title: The Love Letters of Mary Wollstonecraft to Gilbert Imlay
books.author: Mary Wollstonecraft
books.description: A collection of personal correspondence written in the late 18th century. The letters chronicle Wollstonecraft's passionate relationship with Imlay, illustrating her profound emotional struggles and her aspirations for love, family, and personal fulfillment. Wollstonecraft's reflections provide insight into her experiences as a woman navigating the complexities of romance and societal expectations.
