As terrorist attacks plague two galaxies, the children discover their true purpose in an epic battle that will determine Civilization's fate.

books.title: Revolution, and Other Essays
books.author: Jack London
books.description: A collection of essays written in the early 20th century that explores themes of socialism, class struggle, and the human condition. The opening essay, "Revolution," discusses the burgeoning global revolution of the working class, emphasizing the solidarity among millions of socialists united under a common cause to overthrow existing power structures and capitalist societies. The beginning of the book introduces readers to the concept of a world revolution, where millions of "comrades" across various nations rally together, united against their oppressors.

books.title: The Hollow Tree Snowed-in Book
books.subtitle: Being a Continuation of the Stories About the Hollow Tree and Deep Woods People
books.author: Albert Bigelow Paine
books.description: A children's book published in 1910. When a fierce snowstorm traps the 'Coon, the 'Possum, and the Old Black Crow inside their Hollow Tree home in the Deep Woods, the friends pass the time by sharing stories. A storyteller recounts these tales to the Little Lady by the fireplace, bringing to life the adventures and mishaps of these beloved animal characters during their long winter confinement.

books.title: The Brethren
books.author: H. Rider Haggard
books.description: A historical novel written during the late 19th century. It explores themes of chivalry, love, and the intense conflicts between the Crusaders and the Saracens in the Holy Land during the era of the Crusades. The narrative centers around two young knights, Godwin and Wulf D'Arcy, twins of noble blood, as they navigate love and loyalty in a world rife with warfare and impending doom.

books.title: The Humour of Homer and Other Essays
books.author: Samuel Butler
books.description: A collection of essays written in the late 19th century that explores themes related to literature, art, and science, with a particular focus on humor in classical works. The book contains a significant essay titled "The Humour of Homer," which discusses the comedic aspects of Homer's epics, particularly the Iliad and the Odyssey, while also questioning the traditional interpretations and authorship of these texts.

books.title: A Book of Poems, Al Que Quiere!
books.author: William Carlos Williams
books.description: A collection of 52 poems published in 1917. The title translates to "To Him Who Wants It," reflecting Williams's sense of being an unwanted voice in poetry's landscape. In this early work, Williams experiments with various styles while abandoning traditional rhyme, meter, and figurative language. The collection captures a poet finding his voice, offering his work to whoever might want to receive it.

books.title: Annabel
books.subtitle: A Novel for Young Folks
books.author: L. Frank Baum
books.description: A juvenile novel published in 1906 under the pseudonym Suzanne Metcalf. Fifteen-year-old Will Carden has fallen from privilege to poverty, now growing vegetables to support his family. When he saves red-haired Annabel Williams from a frozen pond, an unlikely friendship blooms between the "vegetable boy" and the steel magnate's daughter. But a dark secret involving Will's supposedly dead father threatens everything they know about their families' intertwined past.

books.title: Key Out of Time
books.author: Andre Norton
books.description: While searching a distant world of shallow seas and archipelagos for traces of a galactic civilization, a group of explorers get stranded in the past and face a dangerous enemy.

books.title: The Journal of a Tour to the Hebrides with Samuel Johnson, LL.D.
books.author: James Boswell
books.description: A travel journal published in 1785. The work chronicles Boswell and Samuel Johnson's 1773 journey through the Scottish Highlands and western islands. Based on Boswell's detailed diary entries, the journal captures their conversations and experiences as they traveled from Edinburgh through remote islands including Skye, Coll, and Mull. Known for its anecdotal style and keen attention to detail, the journal served as a preview of Boswell's later masterpiece, his biography of Johnson.

books.title: Robinson Crusoe
books.subtitle: In Words of One Syllable
books.author: Daniel Defoe, Lucy Aikin
books.description: A simplified retelling of the classic novel originally penned by Daniel Defoe, aimed at young readers. This adaptation likely dates back to the early 19th century. The book narrates the adventures of Robinson Crusoe, a shipwrecked sailor who finds himself stranded on a deserted island and must learn to survive amidst challenges and solitude. The opening of this version introduces us to Crusoe's early life, his yearning for adventure, and his initial seafaring experiences that lead to his dramatic shipwreck.

books.title: Israel Potter
books.subtitle: His Fifty Years of Exile
books.author: Herman Melville
books.description: A novel published in 1855. Based on a real Revolutionary War veteran's memoir, it follows Israel Potter from the Battle of Bunker Hill through capture by the British and escape to England. There he encounters King George III, Benjamin Franklin, John Paul Jones, and Ethan Allen in a series of adventures. Despite his patriotic valor, Israel remains exiled in London poverty for decades before finally returning home fifty years later to a changed America.

books.title: The Prince of Parthia
books.subtitle: A Tragedy
books.author: Thomas Godfrey
books.description: A neo-classical tragedy written in the 1760s and first performed in 1767. Set in the ancient Parthian Empire, this groundbreaking play follows Prince Arsaces as he returns victorious from war, only to face deadly intrigue at home. His jealous brother Vardanes, vengeful stepmother Thermusa, and his own father's illicit desires create a web of betrayal and accusations. As political ambition collides with forbidden love, the royal family descends into violence, murder, and tragic misunderstanding.

books.title: The Kellys and the O'Kellys
books.author: Anthony Trollope
books.description: A novel set in mid-19th century Ireland. The narrative explores the complex social dynamics between landlords and tenants, particularly through the experiences of the Kelly family and their connections to the O’Kellys. The story delves into themes of inheritance, love, and the ongoing societal struggles in Ireland during that period. The opening of the story introduces a backdrop of political tension surrounding the trial of prominent figures in the Repeal Movement, setting the stage for the characters' personal and social conflicts.

books.title: Kazan
books.author: James Oliver Curwood
books.description: A novel written in 1914. Part wolf, part husky, Kazan navigates the brutal Canadian wilderness between two worlds—the human civilization that once claimed him and the wild that calls to his blood. After protecting his master's wife from a violent attacker, he flees into the forest, becoming leader of a wolf pack and finding a mate in Gray Wolf. But Kazan's dual nature constantly pulls him between loyalty to humans and the freedom of the wild, leading to encounters with trappers, hunters, and families struggling to survive in the untamed North.

books.title: The Two Admirals
books.author: James Fenimore Cooper
books.description: A nautical fiction novel published in 1842. Set in the 18th-century British Royal Navy, this sea tale emerged from Cooper's publisher encouraging another maritime adventure. Though Cooper's daughter later called it his least successful sea romance, modern critics recognize it as one of his deepest explorations of masculinity. The novel stands among only three of Cooper's works that he chose to revise after their initial printing.

books.title: Captives of the Flame
books.author: Samuel R. Delany
books.description: A science fiction novel written in the early 1960s. The story is set in a dystopian future where the world is on the brink of war, and it follows Jon Koshar, a young man who has recently escaped from a penal camp, as he grapples with his sense of identity and freedom. The novel explores themes of power, societal decay, and the personal struggles of its characters against the backdrop of looming conflict. At the start of the book, the reader is introduced to Jon Koshar as he stumbles through an unfamiliar desert landscape, disoriented after his escape.

books.title: Hand and Ring
books.author: Anna Katharine Green
books.description: Detectives are baffled when a conversation about how to commit the perfect murder is followed within minutes by exactly such a murder.

books.title: Erema
books.subtitle: Or, My Father's Sin
books.author: R. D. Blackmore
books.description: A novel published in 1877. Narrated by fifteen-year-old Erema, the story follows a girl who has grown up in exile with her father in 1850s California. Her father fled England after being wrongly accused of murdering his own father. When he dies, leaving Erema alone, she becomes determined to return to England and clear his name, uncovering the truth behind the crime that destroyed her family.

books.title: The Awkward Age
books.author: Henry James
books.description: A novel first published as a serial in 1898–1899. What begins as a story about a young woman's entry into society becomes a penetrating study of decadence and corruption in English high society. Eighteen-year-old Nanda Brookenham navigates her mother's morally questionable social circle, where hypocrisy and deceit flourish. As marriage prospects and hidden motives intertwine, Nanda must decide whether to embrace or reject the corrupt world around her. Told almost entirely through dialogue, this witty yet unsettling portrait reveals the darker truths beneath sophisticated social gatherings.

books.title: Rachel Ray
books.author: Anthony Trollope
books.description: The attractions of a young woman provoke both admiration and antipathy in her local town.

books.title: Short Fiction
books.author: Vsevolod Garshin
books.description: A collection of Garshin’s translated short stories and novellas ordered by date of publication.

books.title: The Works of Max Beerbohm
books.author: Max Beerbohm
books.description: A collection of satirical essays ridiculing pretentiousness through imitation.

books.title: Béatrix
books.author: Honoré de Balzac
books.description: A young man falls for an older woman, who introduces him to a friend in order to distract him.

books.title: Antic Hay
books.author: Aldous Huxley
books.description: A group of 1920s London socialites struggle with their futures.

books.title: Cogewea, the Half-Blood
books.author: Mourning Dove
books.description: A young woman rancher of mixed Native American and European descent is wooed by the foreman and a newly-arrived tenderfoot.

books.title: The Poisoned Chocolates Case
books.author: Anthony Berkeley
books.description: A club of amateur sleuths attempts to solve a crime whose solution has eluded Scotland Yard.

books.title: Roads to Freedom
books.author: Bertrand Russell
books.description: Bertrand Russell investigates the merits and potential shortcomings of different socialist tendencies.

books.title: Tracks in the Snow
books.author: Godfrey R. Benson
books.description: A rector investigates the mystery behind a strange letter that may be connected to his friend’s murder.

books.title: The Man of Destiny
books.author: George Bernard Shaw
books.description: Napoleon engages in a battle of wits to reclaim some stolen letters.

books.title: Robbery Under Arms
books.author: Rolf Boldrewood
books.description: A young Australian man and his brother are led into a life of crime, becoming cattle stealers, bank robbers and bushrangers before being caught.

books.title: Poetry
books.author: James Weldon Johnson
books.description: A collection of poems by James Weldon Johnson.

books.title: A Daughter of the Samurai
books.author: Etsu Inagaki Sugimoto
books.description: The autobiography of Etsu Sugimoto, a girl born into a samurai family in a time of great cultural changes.

books.title: Captain Jinks, Hero
books.author: Ernest Howard Crosby
books.description: A jingoistic military officer embarks on a tragicomic quest to become a “perfect soldier.”

books.title: The Mystery of the Barranca
books.author: Herman Whitaker
books.description: A mining engineer and his friend suffer a series of misfortunes in their search for riches and treasure.

books.title: Anna of the Five Towns
books.author: Arnold Bennett
books.description: A young woman struggles for independence in the shadow of her domineering father and the rigid conventions of industrial England.

books.title: “We”
books.author: Charles A. Lindbergh
books.description: Legendary aviator Charles Lindbergh gives an account of his early life, how he got into flying, and his famous transatlantic flight.

books.title: The Bridal Wreath
books.author: Sigrid Undset
books.description: In 14th-century Norway, a nobleman’s daughter grows up and faces passion, sin, and filial piety.

books.title: The Turmoil
books.author: Booth Tarkington
books.description: A dreamy and sensitive scion of a Midwestern businessman comes to terms with his legacy in a growing city.

books.title: The Pit-Prop Syndicate
books.author: Freeman Wills Crofts
books.description: A British wine merchant on business in France stumbles across a syndicate with something to hide, and resolves to discover their secret.

books.title: Modeste Mignon
books.author: Honoré de Balzac
books.description: A young daughter seeks independence on her own terms.

books.title: The Necromancers
books.author: Robert Hugh Benson
books.description: A young woman watches with concern as her adopted brother turns to irreligious forces in the hopes of reconnecting with his dead fiancée.

books.title: Those Barren Leaves
books.author: Aldous Huxley
books.description: An aristocrat summons a group of “intelligentsia” to vacation in her Italian mansion.

books.title: Poetry
books.author: Voltairine de Cleyre
books.description: A collection of Voltairine de Cleyre’s poetry.

books.title: Hudibras
books.author: Samuel Butler
books.description: A knight and his squire set forth for adventure and love.

books.title: The Middle Temple Murder
books.author: J. S. Fletcher
books.description: A murder in London’s Middle Temple uncovers a twenty year old conspiracy.

books.title: Hypatia
books.author: Charles Kingsley
books.description: A naive young monk in Roman Alexandria tries to convert a famous pagan woman philosopher to Christianity.

books.title: The Crime at Black Dudley
books.author: Margery Allingham
books.description: The attendees of a party at a old mansion are threatened by a criminal kingpin.

books.title: Short Fiction
books.author: R. A. Lafferty
books.description: A collection of science fiction and fantasy stories by R. A. Lafferty ordered by date of publication.

books.title: The Dark Other
books.author: Stanley G. Weinbaum
books.description: A young woman seeks the reason behind her lover’s outbursts of cruelty.

books.title: The Pit
books.author: Frank Norris
books.description: A couple in turn-of-the-century Chicago navigates the murky waters of greed, ambition, and loss against the backdrop of the Board of Trade’s wheat speculation pits.

books.title: When Charles the First Was King
books.author: J. S. Fletcher
books.description: Serving for the Royalist cause affects the domestic life of a young Yorkshire farmer during the English Civil War.

books.title: The Sport of the Gods
